## Design

### 2026-10-05 – Today I finalized my thoughts for my custom PCB. I am going to make a board that is able to capture IR signals sent from a toy laser gun, translate them, and then out put a master signal to manipulate

**1h**

Today I finalized my thoughts for my custom PCB. I am going to make a board that is able to capture IR signals sent from a toy laser gun, translate them, and then out put a master signal to manipulate the score.

I am going to use an ESP32 as the microcontroller, and some IR leds for signal capture and transmission.

I spent a while editing my idea reel to hopefully gain some traction on youtube.

I also designed a logo for my project, Operation M.I.M.I.C.

### 2026-10-07 – Working on some code, I was able to set up the IRremote library and capture signals from my laser gun. Because the gun uses an unknown signaling scheme, I was not able to translate the code into hexad

**1h**

Working on some code, I was able to set up the IRremote library and capture signals from my laser gun. Because the gun uses an unknown signaling scheme, I was not able to translate the code into hexadecimal. So to be able to replicate the signal, I have to capture the raw timings between on and off.

By setting up components I have on hand on a breadboard, I was able to test my code with an Arduino Uno R3.

![IMG_2951](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Kyb1R5ebGdRzjWmDUY3hYg1WKrU7khl4/b873f1519a111954c429fe296e10f50a26725ffd609cf727dd69be38a5ea0378.png)

I got frustrated when the signals just came back as garbled messes. But after cleaning the data arrays and making sure the library was using timers correctly, I was able to capture a laser blast from one gun, store it, and then fire it at another gun using my own IR led.

![IMG_2952](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Kyb1R5ebGdRzjWmDUY3hYg1WKrU7khl4/85521d638b6ef306a72e5fbe1b6cfd8217b1c9cd74295828622393a054748bdc.png)

Tomorrow I will work on polishing the code and getting it set up with better storage methods on the fly and be able to chose what mode I fire out.
And I will start converting my schematic into a PCB

### 2026-10-08 – While working with the code and testing my temporary ciricut, I reliezed my program is going to be quite complicated. So I started drawing a flow chart.

**1h**

While working with the code and testing my temporary ciricut, I reliezed my program is going to be quite complicated. So I started drawing a flow chart.

![IMG_2960](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Kyb1R5ebGdRzjWmDUY3hYg1WKrU7khl4/c21fb49eff9b8fb6b9fc2c5504045e7078f3fe2d2dcf5936879f7783b1ef8b60.jpg)

This shows some of the main logic of M.I.M.I.C.
The ability to choose the mode via a menu, and cycle though options with just one button. I might add more later if they fit on the pcb just so I can have more inputs.

I also found the LCD screen I want to use. It is small and has only 4 pins so it should fit nicely on the PCB. It also has crisp resolution between the black and white pixels.

![IMG_2961](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Kyb1R5ebGdRzjWmDUY3hYg1WKrU7khl4/f13cd8dde9b98873e041f2560501562ac78a03911b6d8166d0142a3c3d24cc64.jpg)
Tomorrow I have lots of free time so I will do some final hardware tests, then work on designing the PCB. And also finishing round 1 of the firmware.
